text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic received French ambassador to Yugoslavia Stanislas Filiol. The two sides expressed satisfaction with successful development of bilateral cooperation.
- Russian Foreign Minister Yevegeny Primakov says current developments in Yugoslavia are the country's internal affairs and the international community should not interfere.
- Delegation of the Council of Europe visits Belgrade, meets speaker of the lower house of the Yugoslav Parliament Milomir Minic, and deputy foreign minister Zivadin Jovanovic.

- Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce discusses 1997 economic policy, noting the problem of internal debt. The National Bank of Yugoslavia Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic says monetary measures will be more restrictive next year.
- Industrial output up 7.3 percent in November on same month in 1995 says federal statistics office.
- Serbian parliament holds session on Tuesday with the draft on amendments to the law on labour relations taken off its agenda.
- The pro-government Confederation of Autonomous Trade Unions calls for social programme to solve the problem of surplus labour.
- Every people has to fight for its democracy, says Zajedno coalition leader Vesna Pesic at marathon demonstrations in Belgrade over annullment of opposition election results.
- Students continue their protest marches. The students who walked to Belgrade from Nis (230km) are due to arrive Tuesday.
- Over 25,000 people demonstrate in Serbia's southern town of Nis, joined by workers of Machine Industry Nis.
- There will be no printing of money or credits to finance public expenditure, says Serbian Industry Minister Oskar Fodor.

- The steel works Sartid 1913 of Smederevo have an ambitious plan to produce one million tonnes of steel in 1997 basing their forecasts on production pace they have set in last months of 1996, says one of Sartid's managers Zoran Slovic.
